items.excerpt: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory researchers built an AI model that couples thermodynamics with atom-transport kinetics to simulate solid-state reaction pathways in minutes, predicting intermediates, final products and impurities. It reproduced decades of barium-titanium oxide experiments, pointing to faster, higher-purity materials synthesis.

Emory and Georgia Tech researchers built CapuchinAI, a battery-powered field rig that uses facial recognition to identify an approaching wild capuchin, serve a cognitive task tailored to that individual on a touchscreen, and dispense a reward. Field trials hit 97% ID accuracy, opening automated cognition studies outside the lab.

École Normale Supérieure and Institut Pasteur researchers built EscapeMap, a generative AI framework that designs heavily mutated but still functional SARS-CoV-2 spike variants by balancing sequence viability, ACE2 affinity and immune selection. Most AI-generated variants escaped prevalent antibodies, giving a way to stress-test therapeutics against future strains.

AI models have begun knocking down long-standing problems posed by Paul Erdős, and mathematicians are trying to work out why this particular corpus is falling first. The piece treats the Erdős problems as a natural test bed for how far machine-generated proof search can go, and what it means for the rest of math.

University of South Florida and NOAA scientists trained a deep learning model on 1.2 million satellite images to produce the first global assessment of floating algae, revealing blooms spreading across much of the world's ocean. The team links the expansion to shifts in ocean temperature, currents and nutrients.

Medical schools are deciding whether students may use AI scribes that auto-generate clinical notes. Hospitals adopted them to cut burnout, but educators warn that offloading the act of writing a differential removes the cognitive struggle that builds diagnostic reasoning.

Schrödinger CEO Ramy Farid, long a skeptic who bet on physics-based simulation over machine learning, explains what changed his mind about AI in drug discovery. He argues that within five years the field will have a much sharper read on what AI can and cannot do for molecular design.

OpenAI says an internal version of its next-generation Astra model resolved 10 longstanding open problems in mathematics, quantum complexity theory and theoretical computer science, including results on quantum parallel repetition and lattice problems. No detailed proofs or peer review have been released, so the claims await independent scrutiny.

Quantinuum, NVIDIA and Pfizer researchers combined a transformer language model with reinforcement learning to generate molecular ground-state quantum circuits in a single inference step, thousands of times faster than ADAPT-VQE at matching or better accuracy. They demonstrated it on Quantinuum's Helios machine using the drug molecule imipramine.

Tohoku University researchers wired materials databases, machine-learning interatomic potentials, LLMs, AI agents and automated lab workflows into one closed loop for clean-energy materials. Each round of experiments feeds back into the models to guide the next, potentially cutting years off development.

Florida State University engineers built GridFusionX, an AI forecasting system that fuses multiple data streams to predict electricity demand and renewable generation more precisely. Treating the grid as a dynamic puzzle, the model aims to give operators earlier warning and reduce blackout risk.
